items.title: Give every pinned command a content-addressed execution key and run each unique key once
items.context: U-03a / SRC-137A P0-3. The execution key must bind at least real cwd, command spec, explicit inputs/storyFilesHash, effective env, runtime/tool version, and selector-policy digest. Identical keys execute once; an immutable receipt fans out to multiple intents. Each intent still verifies its own selector and must not share one fuzzy PASS. Replay of the B-137a 58-intent pattern must not exceed the true unique-command count.
items.userSees: "The terminal prints `CausalEvidence: intentCount=58 uniqueExecutionKeys=10 commandExecutions=10 cacheHitRate=82%` and 58 selector verdicts, including explicit `selectorMismatch` where applicable."

happy.desc: Run proof-or-stop verification_evidence_batch_add with a 58-intent pinned batch whose canonical identity tuples collapse to exactly 10 distinct execution keys, using deterministic command counters and selectors that match their captured outputs; assert exactly 10 child command executions, one immutable CAS receipt per unique key, 58 independently recorded selector verdicts, intentCount=58, uniqueExecutionKeys=10, commandExecutions=10, cacheHitRate>=80%, and no intent inherits another intent's verdict.

verification.selector: 58 intents fan out from 10 exact execution keys with commandExecutions=10 and independent selector verdicts

happy.desc: Replay the identical 58-intent batch in the same real cwd with unchanged command specs, explicit inputs/storyFilesHash, effective environment, runtime/tool version, and selector-policy digest; assert all 10 exact receipts are reused without changing receipt hashes, the replay performs 0 child command executions, and all 58 selector verdicts remain individually recorded.

verification.selector: exact receipt replay reuses all 10 receipts with commandReruns=0 and preserves per-intent selector verdicts

happy.desc: Submit the same pinned command once through the single-intent path and once in a batch with an exact identity match; assert both resolve to the same execution key and immutable receipt, while the metrics count one unique execution rather than two command runs.

verification.selector: single and batch evidence paths resolve an exact identity to one execution key and one receipt

edge.desc: Starting from one pinned command, vary exactly one execution-key component at a time—real cwd, effective environment, explicit inputs or storyFilesHash, runtime/tool version, and selector-policy digest—while holding all other fields constant; assert every mutation produces a different execution key, a separate immutable receipt, and its own one-time command execution, with no fuzzy or partial-key reuse.

verification.selector: cwd, environment, inputs, runtime version, and selector policy changes each produce distinct execution keys

edge.desc: Fan out one immutable receipt to two intents sharing the exact execution key but using different selectors, with captured output satisfying only one selector; assert the matching intent records PASS, the nonmatching intent records an explicit non-PASS selector verdict with a selector-mismatch reason, and the shared receipt cannot promote the mismatch to PASS.

verification.selector: same receipt yields a matching PASS and a selector-specific non-PASS verdict

edge.desc: Run a batch containing repeated exact keys mixed with near-duplicate keys that differ only in cwd, environment, inputs, or selector policy; assert deduplication occurs only within exact-key groups, metrics report the true uniqueExecutionKeys and commandExecutions, and each group retains independent selector verdicts.

verification.selector: near-duplicate identity groups execute independently while exact-key groups execute once

adversarial.desc: Execute a pinned command, then tamper with the persisted CAS receipt bytes, payload, or receipt hash before replaying the exact key; assert immutable-receipt integrity validation rejects reuse and produces no PASS from altered output (it must fail closed or create a new valid receipt only after a fresh execution), never accepting the tampered receipt.

verification.selector: tampered CAS receipt is rejected and cannot produce PASS

adversarial.desc: Inject a deterministic execution-key or receipt-store collision so two non-identical identity tuples or outputs resolve to the same storage address; assert the collision is detected by canonical identity and receipt validation, the wrong output is never fanned out, and no affected intent receives a false PASS.

verification.selector: execution-key or receipt collision fails closed without false PASS

adversarial.desc: Replay a valid receipt under changed cwd, effective environment, explicit inputs/storyFilesHash, runtime/tool version, selector-policy digest, story, or selector metadata; assert the key/provenance or selector check rejects the replay as non-admissible, does not reuse it as PASS, and records the failure reason without silently increasing coverage.

verification.selector: changed provenance or selector metadata cannot replay a valid receipt as PASS

items.title: Write CAS receipts before canonical evidence import and retry the transaction instead of re-running the command
items.context: U-03a / SRC-137A P0-6 and B-74af. Command results persist as an immutable CAS receipt first. Canonical evidence import/Git commit is a separate atomic transaction. If import or metadata commit fails, retry only that transaction. Command re-executions after a canonical-commit failure must be 0. Receipts must not be rewritten to a new hash.
items.userSees: "The terminal prints `receiptPersistedBeforeCanonicalImport` and, after a simulated commit failure, `importRetry commandRerun=0 receiptHash=<unchanged>`."

happy.desc: Run the causal-evidence test with a valid pinned command and writable canonical evidence target; assert the immutable content-addressed receipt is persisted before the canonical import begins, the receipt hash equals the hash of its stored bytes, the import succeeds, and the canonical evidence record references that exact receipt hash and execution key with commandRerun=0.

verification.selector: receipt-persist event precedes canonical-import event; import PASS references the unchanged CAS receipt hash and commandRerun=0

happy.desc: Import one valid receipt into an empty canonical checklist/evidence store and then repeat the same import with the same story, execution key, receipt hash, lease, and Git base; assert the canonical result is successful and exactly one evidence record is present, with no receipt rewrite or duplicate canonical entry.

verification.selector: first import succeeds and identical import is an idempotent no-duplicate success with one receipt hash

edge.desc: Persist a valid CAS receipt, inject a deterministic Git or metadata commit failure before canonical import commits, clear the failure, and retry only the import transaction; with the original writer lease still valid and the Git index at the expected base, assert eventual canonical import success, commandRerun=0, one canonical record, and a byte-for-byte stable receipt hash.

verification.selector: simulated Git/metadata failure then retry reports importRetry or receiptReuse, commandRerun=0, stable receiptHash, valid lease, and expected Git index

edge.desc: Fail after canonical evidence data is staged but before metadata/index commit, then retry with the same receipt under the same valid lease and expected Git index; assert the retry reconciles the staged transaction exactly once, does not duplicate or overwrite canonical evidence, and never re-executes the command.

verification.selector: staged-before-index failure is recovered idempotently with one canonical import, unchanged receiptHash, and commandRerun=0

edge.desc: Attempt an import retry while the receipt remains valid but the writer lease is expired or the Git index/base has changed; assert pre-import admissibility rejects the transaction with a precise lease-or-index reason, leaves the CAS receipt unchanged, writes no new canonical PASS, and records commandRerun=0.

verification.selector: expired lease or changed Git index fails the import transaction closed without receipt mutation or command rerun

adversarial.desc: Persist a valid receipt, tamper with its stored bytes or declared receipt hash, and attempt canonical import; assert receipt integrity validation rejects it, no canonical PASS or partial evidence is published, the original valid receipt is not overwritten, and commandRerun=0.

verification.selector: tampered CAS receipt fails closed with no canonical import and no receipt overwrite

adversarial.desc: Present a valid receipt under a different execution key or altered command identity/provenance and attempt import; assert the wrong-key receipt is rejected before canonical evidence is committed, no false PASS or index entry is created, and the stored receipt hash remains unchanged.

verification.selector: wrong execution key or provenance fails closed before import and cannot produce PASS

adversarial.desc: Attempt to overwrite an existing CAS address with a different receipt payload or hash while a canonical import references the original receipt; assert the CAS write is rejected as immutable, the original bytes and receipt hash remain stable, and canonical evidence cannot be redirected to the replacement.

verification.selector: receipt-overwrite or same-address different-payload attempt fails closed and preserves the original receipt

adversarial.desc: Force a partial canonical import such as a receipt reference without its required metadata, selector verdict, or Git index entry, then interrupt and retry; assert the incomplete transaction is not reported as success, no partial evidence is exposed as a PASS, the import is rejected or atomically repaired only from the unchanged valid receipt, and commandRerun=0.

verification.selector: partial canonical import fails closed or atomically completes without exposing partial PASS, receipt mutation, or command rerun

items.title: Declare evidence dependency domains and stale only causally affected nodes
items.context: U-03b / SRC-9812 P0-3. Split source, test, build-input, manifest-semantic, integration, and review-subject into declarative domains. Keep materialHash and the current strict fallback. Do not rewrite stored hashes or disguise old output as new evidence. Unrelated merge must not rerun specialized commands; affected DAG nodes rerun at 100% with false-fresh=0. Shadow-compare first, then let CertificationWindow do precise invalidation. DONE-required whole-tree drift remains on the current strict policy.
items.userSees: "The terminal prints `causalDecision=advisory specializedRerun=0` for unrelated drift and `affectedNodeRerun=100% falseFresh=0` for related drift; DONE-required validation remains `strict`."

happy.desc: Run the causal-evidence integration test with declarative source, test, build-input, manifest-semantic, integration, and review-subject nodes; first apply a merge that changes only an unrelated whole-tree file and assert the specialized evidence receipts remain admissible, specializedRerun=0, causalDecision=advisory, and no stored dependency or material hash is rewritten.

verification.selector: B-5a15|CHK-003:happy:0|PASS|unrelated merge preserves specialized evidence with specializedRerun=0, explicit advisory, and unchanged stored hashes

happy.desc: In the same DAG, change a story-owned source or build input that a specialized node declares, recompute the causal decision, and assert every affected node and its declared downstream dependents rerun exactly once at affectedNodeRerun=100%, unaffected specialized nodes do not rerun, and falseFresh=0.

verification.selector: B-5a15|CHK-003:happy:1|PASS|related story-owned material change invalidates the affected transitive closure, reruns it at 100%, and reports falseFresh=0

happy.desc: Pass the shadow-compare result into CertificationWindow for both cases and assert the window consumes the signed causal decision: it retains the specialized evidence for the unrelated merge as advisory, but requires fresh evidence for the related affected nodes before admitting a gate PASS.

verification.selector: B-5a15|CHK-003:happy:2|PASS|CertificationWindow accepts only the causal decision and admits no stale affected-node PASS

edge.desc: Mutate one representative input at a time for source, test, build-input, manifest-semantic, integration, and review-subject domains while holding all other files constant; assert the node in the changed domain and only its declared dependents become stale, while nodes in the other five domains remain fresh and specialized reruns are not broadened by fuzzy matching.

verification.selector: B-5a15|CHK-003:edge:0|PASS|each of the six dependency domains has a distinct invalidation boundary and only the declared dependent closure is stale

edge.desc: Exercise a legacy or incomplete dependency declaration with a materialHash change that cannot be attributed to a declared domain; assert the current strict materialHash fallback marks the evidence stale, refuses reuse as PASS, preserves the old stored hash, and reports falseFresh=0 rather than guessing that the change is unrelated.

verification.selector: B-5a15|CHK-003:edge:1|PASS|missing or ambiguous domain metadata falls back to strict materialHash invalidation with no false-fresh reuse

edge.desc: Use semantically similar but distinct changes—test-only versus build-input, manifest-semantic versus integration, and review-subject versus source—and assert each pair produces different dependency hashes and decisions, with no cross-domain aliasing and no rerun of a specialized command whose declared inputs are unchanged.

verification.selector: B-5a15|CHK-003:edge:2|PASS|nearby changes in test/build-input, manifest/integration, and review/source remain domain-distinct

adversarial.desc: Forge a fresh-looking dependency record by omitting a changed story-owned input or supplying the prior domain hash after the material change; assert shadow-compare detects the mismatch, the affected node is stale, the old output cannot produce PASS, and falseFresh remains 0.

verification.selector: B-5a15|CHK-003:adversarial:0|PASS|forged or omitted dependency hashes are rejected by shadow compare and cannot create a fresh gate PASS

adversarial.desc: Attempt to rewrite a stored evidence hash, dependency hash, materialHash, or receipt provenance to match the current tree after a related change; assert content-addressed evidence is immutable, the rewrite is rejected or ignored, the original bytes and hashes remain stable, and no old output is reclassified as fresh.

verification.selector: B-5a15|CHK-003:adversarial:1|PASS|content-addressed dependency and receipt provenance rewrite is rejected and original hashes remain stable

adversarial.desc: Invoke CertificationWindow with a stale affected node while presenting a valid-looking causal advisory, or bypass the causal decision and submit the old specialized PASS directly; assert the window rejects the bypass, does not downgrade a related invalidation to advisory, and emits no gate-admissible PASS.

verification.selector: B-5a15|CHK-003:adversarial:2|PASS|CertificationWindow bypass is rejected and a stale affected PASS cannot enter a gate

adversarial.desc: Run the DONE-required validation path after an unrelated whole-tree merge that the specialized DAG classifies as advisory; assert the current strict whole-tree policy still marks DONE-required evidence stale or blocks DONE, so causal specialization cannot waive the DONE gate.

items.context: U-03 optimization bullet: before an expensive run, check CLI/worktree, Git index, writer/lease, provider capability, resources, and that the evidence target is writable. Fail closed with a precise error instead of starting a 93-command suite that cannot persist. This is a preflight, not a freshness relaxation.
items.userSees: "The terminal prints `preflight REFUSED: <failed_check_reason> commandExecutions=0` and no child-launch event when CLI, worktree, index, lease, capability, resources, or evidence target is invalid."

happy.desc: Run the expensive-run preflight in a canonical story worktree with the expected CLI available, a readable and unchanged Git index, a valid writer identity and unexpired lease, a provider that advertises every required capability, sufficient resource budget, and a writable evidence target; assert the report names all seven checks as PASS, the preflight PASS event precedes child-launch, exactly one child command starts only after that event, and the resulting evidence is persisted.

verification.selector: expensive-run preflight PASS: cli=pass worktree=pass gitIndex=pass writerLease=pass providerCapability=pass resources=pass evidenceTarget=pass; childLaunch=1

happy.desc: Run a valid expensive batch twice without changing the CLI, worktree, Git index, writer lease, provider capability, resource budget, or evidence target; assert both preflights complete before any child launch, the first run launches and persists normally, and the second run reuses the same admissible preflight contract without launching a child before preflight or creating duplicate evidence.

verification.selector: repeated valid preflight remains PASS-before-launch with one committed evidence result and no duplicate child launch

edge.desc: Remove or make unavailable the configured Proof-or-Stop CLI used to start the expensive run while leaving the other inputs valid; assert preflight refuses with the exact cli_unavailable reason, identifies the missing executable, records commandExecutions=0, and leaves the evidence target and Git index unchanged.

verification.selector: preflight REFUSED: cli_unavailable; commandExecutions=0

edge.desc: Invoke the expensive run from a non-canonical directory or a different story worktree while the CLI and all remaining checks are valid; assert preflight refuses with the exact worktree_mismatch reason naming expected and actual paths, records commandExecutions=0, and launches no child.

verification.selector: preflight REFUSED: worktree_mismatch; commandExecutions=0

edge.desc: Make the expected Git index missing, unreadable, locked, or based on a different HEAD/index identity; assert preflight refuses with a precise git_index_unavailable or git_index_mismatch reason naming the failed condition, records commandExecutions=0, and does not stage, commit, or alter evidence.

verification.selector: preflight REFUSED: git_index_unavailable or git_index_mismatch; commandExecutions=0

edge.desc: Run without a registered writer identity or with a writer identity that lacks permission for the story evidence target; assert preflight refuses with the exact writer_unavailable reason, records commandExecutions=0, and leaves lease, index, and evidence state unchanged.

verification.selector: preflight REFUSED: writer_unavailable; commandExecutions=0

edge.desc: Use an expired, revoked, mismatched, or already-owned writer lease while all other preflight inputs are valid; assert preflight refuses with the exact lease_invalid reason identifying the lease failure, records commandExecutions=0, and does not renew, steal, or mutate the lease as a side effect.

verification.selector: preflight REFUSED: lease_invalid; commandExecutions=0

edge.desc: Configure a provider that cannot execute the required command kind, lacks the required capability, or reports an incompatible runtime contract; assert preflight refuses with the exact provider_capability_missing reason naming the missing capability, records commandExecutions=0, and does not fall back to an unapproved provider.

verification.selector: preflight REFUSED: provider_capability_missing; commandExecutions=0

edge.desc: Set the required timeout, memory, disk, or concurrency budget below the expensive run’s declared resource requirement; assert preflight refuses with the exact insufficient_resources reason naming the failed resource and required versus available values, records commandExecutions=0, and does not reserve or consume a child slot.

verification.selector: preflight REFUSED: insufficient_resources; commandExecutions=0

edge.desc: Point the evidence target at a missing parent, read-only location, non-directory collision, or path that cannot be created or atomically written; assert preflight refuses with the exact evidence_target_not_writable reason naming the target and failed write probe, records commandExecutions=0, and writes no partial evidence or receipt.

verification.selector: preflight REFUSED: evidence_target_not_writable; commandExecutions=0

adversarial.desc: Make every preflight check pass, then change the worktree, Git index, writer lease, provider capability, resource budget, or evidence target in the gap before child launch; assert an atomic revalidation catches the race, refuses with state_changed_before_launch, records commandExecutions=0, and writes no evidence, receipt, index entry, or child-side artifact.

verification.selector: preflight RACE REFUSED: state_changed_before_launch; commandExecutions=0; evidenceWrites=0

adversarial.desc: Attempt to bypass the preflight by omitting it, replaying a stale PASS, forging individual check results, changing the target after the PASS, or invoking the child runner through a lower-level path; assert the launch gate rejects the missing, stale, or forged preflight contract, records commandExecutions=0, and cannot produce a gate-admissible evidence PASS.

verification.selector: B-5a15|CHK-004:adversarial:1|PASS|missing, stale, or forged preflight is rejected before child launch with commandExecutions=0 and no gate-admissible PASS

items.title: Report U-03 correctness and efficiency metrics without reducing assurance
items.context: Section 12 of the plan: every optimization Story must report correctness invariants and efficiency. Required after-metrics include unique commands vs executions, exact-input cache hit rate (target >= 80%, stale cache acceptance = 0), command reruns after commit failure = 0, unrelated specialized rerun = 0, affected-node rerun = 100%, false-fresh = 0. Do not reduce reviewer lanes, hide coverage with waivers, or call the Story done while phase is not DONE.
